title: Dry Screw Vacuum Pump
model_title: Dry Screw Vacuum Pump (Variable-Pitch Screws, Timing Gears)

introduction.definition: A dry screw vacuum pump uses two non-contacting screw rotors, synchronised by timing gears, to carry gas from the inlet to the exhaust. Variable pitch compresses the gas internally. There is no oil or liquid in the gas path, so the process is not contaminated.
key_points: Handles condensables with purge and temperature control
introduction.summary: A dry screw vacuum pump has two parallel screw rotors that mesh without touching, synchronised by timing gears. Gas trapped in the threads is moved from the inlet (vacuum side) to the exhaust; a shorter pitch toward the exhaust compresses it internally. No oil or water is in the gas path, so the gas is not contaminated — ideal for chemical, pharmaceutical and semiconductor processes.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Fit inlet trap/condenser for heavy vapour loads; provide nitrogen purge and cooling water.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

video_tutorials.title: Dry Screw Vacuum Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Dry Screw Vacuum Pump.
A dry screw vacuum pump uses two non-contacting screw rotors, synchronised by timing gears, to carry gas from the inlet to the exhaust.
Variable pitch compresses the gas internally.
There is no oil or liquid in the gas path, so the process is not contaminated.
Typical applications include chemical and pharmaceutical processes (distillation, drying); semiconductor and solar manufacturing; vacuum degassing, coating; solvent recovery.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Stator Casing (water-cooled) — Inlet top, Exhaust bottom, Drive Screw Rotor (pitch decreases toward exhaust), Driven Screw Rotor (pitch decreases toward exhaust).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Dry Screw Vacuum Pump works.
Gas enters the inlet at the vacuum end.
Gas trapped in the threads is moved along by the counter-rotating screws.
Shorter pitch near the exhaust compresses the gas internally.
Timing gears keep the screws in step without contact.
Gas exhausts near atmospheric pressure.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Gas trapped in the screw threads is carried from the vacuum (inlet) end to the exhaust; the shorter pitch near the exhaust compresses it internally up to slightly above atmospheric pressure.

video_tutorials.title: Dry Screw Vacuum Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Dry Screw Vacuum Pump.
Check cooling water and purge flow; motor current trend.
Flush with solvent if deposits are expected.
Replace bearings and gear oil; inspect screws.
Watch for deposits / seizure: rising current, trips. Common cause: process polymerises or condenses inside.
Watch for overheating: high casing temperature. Common cause: cooling-water loss.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
